job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today I visited my uncle’s farm, and I learned so much about agriculture. I saw him preparing the soil by ploughing, which loosens the earth to allow roots to breathe deeply and improves nutrient circulation. He explained that we must add manure, which is organic matter from decomposed waste, to enrich the soil naturally rather than relying solely on chemical fertilizers. I also watched him sort seeds by placing them in water; the healthy, heavy seeds sank, while the hollow, damaged ones floated. He told me that we must never store grains while they are moist, as moisture encourages fungal growth and spoilage. Instead, grains must be dried thoroughly in the sun before storage. We also talked about weeds, which are unwanted plants that compete with crops for water, nutrients, and sunlight, potentially reducing our yield significantly. Finally, he showed me the drip irrigation system. Unlike flooding the whole field, which wastes water, drip irrigation delivers water directly to the base of the roots, ensuring the plant gets exactly what it needs without unnecessary loss. It is fascinating how much science goes into growing our food properly!
response.summary: The passage explains essential agricultural practices including soil preparation, seed selection, and proper storage. It also highlights the importance of managing weeds and using efficient irrigation methods for healthy crop growth.
